title: Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a measurement platform that repeatedly follows many identified molecules, their states and their interactions inside the same living cell. It would combine molecular identification with subcellular location and time, allowing researchers to observe how a cell changes during a biological event while preserving its ability to function. The intended capability goes beyond recognizing organelles: it would distinguish a broad, validated panel of molecular targets and measure changes in their abundance, state or relationships.

Conceptual synthesis: the motivating problem is a tradeoff among molecular breadth, spatial detail, measurement speed and biological disturbance. The supplied research describes comprehensive assays as often consuming or fixing cells, while live imaging typically follows a limited set of labels. That account motivates the innovation, but the supplied evidence does not independently establish how broadly it applies across existing methods. The objective is therefore a substantial expansion of repeated molecular observation, without implying that every molecule or every interaction could be observed.

significance.text: Conditional impact: successful measurement would reveal molecular trajectories within individual cells, connecting earlier states to later events instead of assembling those relationships solely from separate cells or separate measurements. Following multiple targets together could show which changes precede, accompany or follow an event and expose differences between cells that would disappear in population averages. The revolutionary advance would be the combination of molecular breadth, repeated observation and preserved biological function.

Conditional downstream possibilities include better experiments on cellular regulation and richer data for predictive cell models. Observation alone would not establish why an event occurred: correlated molecular changes can share an upstream cause, and measurements can omit relevant variables. An experimentally predictive virtual cell would still require causal perturbations, suitable models and validation on outcomes beyond the observations used to build it.

Impact synthesis: routine laboratory access would extend the capability beyond specialist facilities, but affordability, usability and availability are proposed requirements rather than demonstrated properties. The analogy to a comprehensive view of the cell also has limits. A broad panel remains a selected panel, an image does not automatically identify a molecular state, and spatial proximity does not by itself establish a biochemical interaction.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable, repeated measurement of a broad molecular panel throughout an individual living cell, with enough spatial and temporal detail to resolve the biological events being studied. Molecular identity, abundance, state and interaction are distinct measurement tasks. Recognizing a compartment cannot substitute for identifying its molecular contents, and tracking a labeled protein does not automatically reveal its activity or binding partners.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing platform would need to distinguish many targets despite overlapping signals and the crowded cellular environment, maintain calibration as cells move and change shape, and distinguish real molecular changes from measurement noise. It would also need to balance measurement speed, spatial coverage and signal quality. An event that changes faster than the sampling interval, or occurs outside the observed volume, could be missed even when the measured targets are correctly identified.

Engineering synthesis: biological compatibility is part of the breakthrough. Labels, probes, illumination and repeated sampling could alter the processes being observed, so apparent viability alone would be an insufficient demonstration of limited disturbance. Computational reconstruction introduces a further challenge: inferred molecular identities or interactions must be validated independently, with uncertainty reported, rather than treated as direct observations merely because a reconstruction produces a plausible image.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies Zhanghao, Li et al., “Fast segmentation and multiplexing imaging of organelles in live cells,” with a reported publication date of March 21, 2025, and DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-57877-5. It attributes segmentation of up to 15 subcellular structures and tracking of interactions among six compartments to the PubMed abstract and figure captions. These bibliographic details and numerical results remain reports from the research input: the retained artifact examined in the supplied review contains only a cookie challenge and cannot independently confirm them.

The earlier research states that the publisher page could not be opened and that its assessment used an accessible abstract and figure captions. The supplied review found neither the abstract nor captions in the retained PubMed artifact. Consequently, this record cannot establish the experimental conditions, measurement accuracy, cell types, temporal performance or biological disturbance associated with the reported counts. The access limitation does not demonstrate that the reported results are false.

Scope synthesis: if demonstrated as described, segmentation of 15 structures and tracking among six compartments would establish useful organelle-level capability. Those counts would not establish simultaneous measurement of 15 molecular species, a broad protein inventory, molecular activity states or validated biochemical interactions. The distinction concerns what was measured; it does not diminish the potential value of organelle imaging.

The supplied material does not establish a demonstration of the full BIO-10 capability. Its empty freshness record also leaves subsequent progress through November 1, 2026 unassessed, and present availability cannot be inferred. These limits concern the coverage and accessibility of the supplied evidence; they do not establish that later advances are absent.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: repeatedly quantify a predefined, independently verified panel of proteins, molecular states and interactions throughout individual living cells during specified biological events. Before testing, define the panel size and composition, the fraction of the cell measured, spatial resolution, sampling interval, observation duration and acceptable error rates. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established field standards; the supplied material does not justify a universal numerical threshold for completion.
completion_criteria.label: Repeatedly quantify verified molecular panels during events in living cells

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: evaluate molecular identification, abundance estimates, state assignments and interaction calls separately against suitable independent measurements or controls. Report missed targets, false identifications, uncertainty and failures as well as successful examples. Distinguish direct measurements from computational estimates, and test whether the platform resolves the timing and location of events relevant to its stated use.
completion_criteria.label: Independently validate molecular measurements and report errors and uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed biological compatibility test: compare measured cells with appropriate controls over the observation period and afterward. Assess the functions relevant to the experiment, alongside survival, to determine whether labeling and measurement materially change the observed process. Specify acceptable disturbance in advance for each use case; a cell remaining alive does not by itself show that its molecular dynamics were preserved.
completion_criteria.label: Measurement preserves relevant cellular functions within predefined disturbance limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce performance across multiple cell types, biological events, operators and independent laboratories, and disclose where performance deteriorates. Demonstrate a usable workflow with documented preparation requirements, analysis effort, costs and instrument access. Such tests would establish demonstrated breadth within stated conditions, not literal universality across all cells, molecules or events.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce performance across settings with documented workflow requirements and limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” is the closest downstream complement. BIO-10 could provide trajectories and validation data, while BIO-04 requires a model that predicts experimental outcomes. BIO-03, “Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts,” could likewise use molecular observations to connect sequence changes to cellular responses. Neither predictive goal follows automatically from improved measurement.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins,” overlaps through observing responses to perturbations, but causal function requires experiments beyond observation. BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” and BIO-15, “Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body,” could use intracellular measurements to evaluate activity or cellular response; enzyme design and selective delivery remain separate capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-01, “Build an autonomously reproducing cell from defined components,” could benefit from tracking molecular processes during construction and reproduction. BIO-02, “Demonstrate a plausible chemical transition from nonlife to evolution,” BIO-11, “Reconstruct the major steps in the origin of eukaryotic cells,” and BIO-12, “Explain how biological homochirality could emerge and persist,” address origins and mechanisms that present-day intracellular observation alone cannot establish. BIO-10 could support selected experiments without supplying those historical or chemical explanations.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-06, “Enable complete, patterned regeneration of complex mammalian structures,” BIO-07, “Reversibly restore youthful function across an aged organism,” and BIO-08, “Make major cereal crops reliably obtain most of their nitrogen biologically,” could benefit from observing relevant cellular processes. Their completion depends on coordinated tissue, organism or crop performance, extending well beyond a measurement platform.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-09, “Observe and causally test whole-brain computation at cellular resolution,” shares the challenge of broad observation with limited disturbance, but emphasizes activity across many cells and causal tests of computation. BIO-13, “Establish the physical mechanisms that store and retrieve a long-term memory,” could draw on molecular measurements within relevant cells, but requires linking those mechanisms to memory storage and retrieval. BIO-10 focuses on molecular detail inside cells rather than establishing either brain-wide computation or memory mechanisms.

brief.title: Watching molecules change inside living cells
possible: Researchers could follow many identified molecules inside the same living cell as an event unfolds. They could see where the molecules are, how much is present, what state they are in and how they interact, while the cell continues to function.
why: Following a cell over time would connect its earlier molecular changes to later events. Researchers could see which changes come before, during or after an event, including differences between cells that disappear when results are averaged.
These observations could improve experiments on how cells regulate themselves and provide richer data for models that predict cell behaviour.

sources.who: Karl Zhanghao, Meiqi Li and collaborators
sources.showed: They used a membrane-staining dye and image analysis to distinguish organelles, the compartments inside cells, and follow their changing relationships in living cells.
sources.quote: we successfully segmented up to 15 subcellular structures
sources.cited_for: The work supports observing many cellular compartments together over time.
sources.not_established: Recognising compartments does not establish the identities, states or biochemical interactions of their molecular contents.

sources.who: Yong Qian, Orhan T. Celiker, Zeguan Wang, Burcu Guner-Ataman and Edward S. Boyden
sources.showed: They separated glowing labels by how their brightness changed over time. This let ordinary microscopes follow multiple signals within the same living cell.
sources.quote:

than are feasible with traditional spectral multiplexing on a conven-
tional microscope using fully genetically encoded reagents,
sources.cited_for: The work supports following molecular signals together, including protein activity and changes during cell division.
sources.not_established: The demonstrations do not establish repeated measurement of a broad molecular panel throughout a cell with preserved function.

sources.who: Anthony R. Braun and collaborators at the University of Minnesota
sources.showed: They built light-based sensors for protein interactions and changes in protein shape. Under carefully adjusted conditions, signals could be separated within the same cell.
sources.quote: We first establish that MDF fluorophores exhibit minimal background FRET under co-expression, enabling clean separation of donor lifetimes under multiplexed conditions.
sources.cited_for: The work supports measuring selected molecular relationships rather than only locating cellular compartments.
sources.not_established: Selected sensors do not establish broad molecular coverage, and producing too much of a monitored protein could disturb cells.

sources.who: Morgan Richards, Qiyin Fang and collaborators
sources.showed: They built a faster microscope that measures how long fluorescent labels glow after excitation, including labels used to sense molecular interactions in living cells.
sources.quote: These efficiency improvements are leveraged by redesigning the optomechanical system and software processing to achieve a frame rate 12 times faster than previously demonstrated.
sources.cited_for: The work supports faster measurements of molecular changes inside living cells.
sources.not_established: Faster imaging alone does not establish broad molecular identification or preserved cellular function during repeated observation.

shown: Zhanghao, Li and collaborators distinguished many cellular compartments and followed their dynamics. Qian and colleagues followed seven signals in individual living cells, bringing simultaneous observation closer to molecular activity.

Braun and colleagues measured selected protein relationships within the same cell under optimised conditions. Richards and colleagues accelerated imaging of molecular sensors. These demonstrations address different parts of the larger capability.
missing: A broad, independently checked set of molecules, states and interactions still needs to be followed repeatedly throughout individual living cells.
Measurements need enough speed and spatial coverage to capture the events being studied, with errors distinguished from real changes.
Repeated observation must preserve the cellular functions under study, beyond keeping cells alive.
Performance and practical requirements need to hold across cell types, events, operators and independent laboratories.

milestones.label: Verified molecular measurements throughout living-cell events
milestones.explanation: A platform would have to repeatedly measure a predefined set of proteins, states and interactions during specified events, with coverage and performance defined beforehand. This would establish the core capability.

milestones.label: Independent checks establish accuracy and uncertainty
milestones.explanation: Independent tests would have to assess molecular identity, quantity, state and interaction separately, reporting errors and distinguishing measurements from estimates. This would establish which results deserve confidence.

milestones.label: Measured cells preserve the functions being studied
milestones.explanation: Comparisons with control cells would have to show that relevant functions remain within predefined disturbance limits during and after observation. This would establish that measurement preserves the process being studied.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce performance across settings
milestones.explanation: Performance would have to repeat across cell types, events, operators and independent laboratories, with workflow requirements and limits documented. This would establish where the capability works and how others could use it.

uncertain: The necessary molecular breadth, coverage, speed, observation duration and acceptable error depend on the biological question.
Acceptable disturbance must be defined for each use; survival alone cannot establish normal cellular behaviour.
Molecules changing together may share another cause, and proximity alone does not establish a biochemical interaction.

page.title: Systems-level live-cell molecular imaging
page.definition: A platform repeatedly measures the locations, abundances, activity states and interactions of the molecular components of one experimentally defined signaling network in the same living cell. A signaling network comprises molecules that relay and regulate cellular responses; measurement preserves the process under study.

goal.need: Qian et al. describe conventional spectral imaging as usually limited to 2–3 signals, occasionally four. Increasing molecular coverage must also preserve cell function: Laissue et al. observed reduced proliferation of unlabeled Vero cells after 4–5 minutes of blue-light exposure, corresponding to 18.5–23.1 J/cm². The goal combines molecular coverage with repeated observation of cellular responses.

completion.title: An independent laboratory reproduces molecular imaging of an entire specified signaling network.
completion.criterion: An independent laboratory reproduces same-cell time series covering the prespecified component-and-interaction inventory of an experimentally defined signaling network, including subcellular location, abundance and relevant activity states. Molecular identities and interaction readouts agree with independent assays; sampling resolves the response to a specified perturbation; the cellular process under study passes an experiment-specific functional preservation test. The inventory, sampling requirements and assay acceptance limits must be published before replication. No universal numerical minimum is asserted.
completion.set_by: Atlas; an operational interpretation of the published network-imaging objective, rather than an externally adopted acceptance test.
completion.basis: Searches of NIH Follow that Cell prize rules, DOE characterization roadmaps, CZI Dynamic Imaging calls and microscopy assessment guidance found no joint acceptance test for molecular coverage, states, interactions, timing and preserved function. This Atlas criterion bounds coverage by one defined network, following Janelia's stated objective, and requires reproduction of the integrated result. It is not a field standard.

milestones.title: The same living cell yields molecular time series over a biologically significant interval.
milestones.criterion: Obtain time courses from the same living cell over a biologically significant interval, with sampling appropriate to the process; NIH specifies no universal duration or interval. Published result: on 7 December 2023, Qian et al. reported four kinase-activity reporters sampled every 2 min for 1 h in NIH/3T3 cells; the bFGF2 stimulation experiment used 30 cells from two cultures. This demonstrates time-series acquisition.
milestones.set_by: NIH Common Fund, Follow that Cell Challenge, Phase 2 time-course measurement criterion; this is one prize criterion, not the complete prize-winning test.
milestones.threshold_quote: Must provide time course measurement data on the same cell over a biologically significant period of time with adequate time intervals.

milestones.title: Multiple molecular species are measured together with spatial and temporal resolution.
milestones.criterion: Measure multiple molecular species together with spatial and temporal resolution appropriate to their activity; DOE specifies no minimum species count or universal resolution. Published results: Qian et al. imaged seven signaling readouts in nine NIH/3T3 cells from two cultures. Braun et al., published on 6 February 2026, resolved two TNF-receptor conformation biosensors in co-expressing HEK293T cells, with three biological replicates. These are selected readouts rather than an entire network inventory.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Department of Energy, New Frontiers in Characterizing Biological Systems, section 4.1.1; a qualitative capability target for DOE-relevant biological systems.
milestones.threshold_quote: spatially map the activity of multiple cellular processes in situ.

milestones.title: Imaging stays below the sample-specific threshold for detectable phototoxicity.
milestones.criterion: Acquire the molecular time series within the illumination range where a sample-specific biological assay detects no phototoxicity, established using an illumination dose–response curve. The guidance specifies no universal light dose or equivalence margin. Published result: Qian et al. detected no increase in reactive oxygen species during their 1 h kinase-imaging protocol, comparing 25 illuminated NIH/3T3 cells from two cultures with 18 dark-control cells from one culture. This tests one stress readout, not preservation of every cellular function.
milestones.set_by: Laissue and colleagues, Nature Methods microscopy assessment guidance, drawing on established sample-specific biological assays.
milestones.threshold_quote: phototoxicity cannot be detected with the chosen assessment criterion (or criteria). Biological imaging experiments should be carried out in this regime.

milestones.title: One laboratory images the complete specified network while preserving the cellular process under study.
milestones.criterion: One laboratory demonstrates the integrated network inventory, independently checked molecular readouts and functional preservation required by completion, before replication elsewhere. Partial results: Zhanghao et al., published on 21 March 2025, segmented up to 15 subcellular structures and filmed six structures with three independent replicates; these are compartments rather than a molecular inventory. Richards et al., published on 26 May 2025, demonstrated live-cell fluorescence-lifetime imaging at 4 Hz and 960 × 960 pixels in HEK293T cells; the biological replicate count was unspecified. Neither paper establishes this integrated result.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; no integrated-prototype acceptance test was found in the NIH, DOE or CZI documents examined.

not_found: No external joint completion test or integrated-prototype acceptance test was found for the combined capability.
The 2017 DOE characterization workshop PDF exceeded the web reader's size limit.

results.detail: The segmented structures are organelles and other compartments, not an inventory of the molecular components and interactions of a specified signaling network. Functional preservation was not established.
results.quote: We succeeded in resolving the 3D anatomic structure of live cells at different mitotic phases and tracking the fast dynamic interactions among six intracellular compartments with high robustness.
